label: The relevant CI jobs use the ubuntu-latest runner label, while their workflow commands do not pass a worker cap; the inspected Vitest configs enable file parallelism but do not pin maxWorkers or maxThreads. The workflow files therefore do not record the effective CPU or worker count for a run. The reported deep-loop run spends about 265 seconds in its serial group out of 504-511 seconds total, or roughly 52-53%. Even if the remaining parallel portion were eliminated, that split puts an approximate 1.9x upper bound on file-parallelism speedup for that measured run; raising worker count cannot shorten the serial 12-file group. The parallel groups create per-file worker processes and scratch databases; deep-loop tests also create per-file scratch database roots, and the config notes heavy tests slow down when they share the disk. On a smaller runner, more workers can therefore trade CPU parallelism against disk contention, worker startup, and timing-test noise; the source does not show a linear gain. No small-runner timing is recorded: all packet timings are from one 18-core Mac. Before changing worker count, capture the actual CI runner’s available processors, memory, OS/Node/Vitest versions, then compare the exact CI commands at fixed caps such as 1, 2, 4, and default across repeated runs. Keep file lists and assertion counts fixed; record lane and per-file wall time, CPU/RSS, temp-database and lock contention, timeouts, and failures. Use the median and spread to choose a setting; keep the timing-sensitive serial group unchanged unless separate evidence proves a safe split.
